title: Container build broken on macOS: CAM-178 uid re-home fails (groupmod -n renames name but never frees the colliding GID)
description: The CAM-178 re-home block in .devcontainer/Dockerfile fails at build time whenever the host GID collides with an existing group in the oven/bun:1.2-slim base. On macOS host gid=20 (staff) collides with dialout:x:20 in the base. The collision guard runs `groupmod -n dialout dialout_rehomed` (renames the NAME) then `groupmod -g 20 bun`, which FAILS with `groupmod: GID 20 already exists` because renaming a group does NOT free its gid — dialout_rehomed still owns gid 20. Reproduced empirically: docker build --build-arg HOST_UID=501 --build-arg HOST_GID=20 fails at step 7/8 (exit 4). The cached cam-worker:latest still has bun uid=1000 gid=1000 (re-home never succeeded here), so the EACCES on /workspace that CAM-178 was meant to fix is STILL present on this host. Production hits the same path: resolveHostIds returns id -u=501/id -g=20 and threads the identical build-args. Never caught because CI (macos-latest) has no Docker daemon and the tests are argv-builders; CAM-178 shipped host-mode autonomous with no real docker build ever run. FIX (recommended): stop trying to renumber the colliding group. Branch on whether HOST_GID already exists: if it exists, set bun’s primary group to it by gid (usermod -u HOST_UID -g HOST_GID bun) — group NAME is irrelevant since chown -R uses numeric HOST_UID:HOST_GID; if it does NOT exist, groupmod -g HOST_GID bun then usermod -u HOST_UID bun. Blocks CAM-180 (cannot build image to verify CAM-179 onboarding) and all downstream container-mode work (CAM-176, CAM-175 re-run, CAM-139). VERIFICATION MUST include a real docker build on a macOS host (gid=20), not just argv unit tests — asserting bun ends at uid=501 gid=20 and /workspace is writable.

spec.scope: Rewrite the CAM-178 uid/gid re-home RUN block in .devcontainer/Dockerfile so the cam-worker image builds on a macOS host where HOST_GID=20 collides with the base image's existing gid-20 group. Replace the group-rename approach (renames the colliding group's NAME via `groupmod -n ${COLLIDING}_rehomed`, which never frees its GID, so `groupmod -g 20 bun` fails with 'GID 20 already exists') with a getent branch: if a group already owns HOST_GID, run `usermod -u HOST_UID -g HOST_GID bun` (set bun's primary group by numeric gid; group NAME is irrelevant because chown uses numeric HOST_UID:HOST_GID); otherwise run `groupmod -g HOST_GID bun` then `usermod -u HOST_UID bun`; keep the trailing `chown -R HOST_UID:HOST_GID /home/bun`. Add a deterministic Dockerfile-text regression test (bun test, no Docker daemon) asserting the new block shape and the removal of the group-rename. OUT OF SCOPE (autonomous): HOST_UID collision handling (neither 501 nor 1000 collides with a pre-existing user on oven/bun:1.2-slim) is a documented risk, not a fix; the real docker-build verification is an operator ceremony (requires:operator), hand-filed after the PRD and folded into the combined CAM-178/183 + CAM-179 + CAM-180 rebuild ceremony; CAM-176 firewall wiring and CAM-179 onboarding (already shipped) are separate issues.
acceptanceCriteria: The .devcontainer/Dockerfile re-home RUN block contains no `groupmod -n` and no `_rehomed` group-name rename; the collision-guard-by-rename is removed.

The re-home block branches on `getent group "$HOST_GID"`: when the group exists it runs `usermod -u "$HOST_UID" -g "$HOST_GID" bun`; when it does not it runs `groupmod -g "$HOST_GID" bun` then `usermod -u "$HOST_UID" bun`.

The block still ends with `chown -R "$HOST_UID:$HOST_GID" /home/bun`; the `ARG HOST_UID=1000` / `ARG HOST_GID=1000` defaults and the `COPY .devcontainer/claude-config.json /home/bun/.claude.json` positioned BEFORE `ARG HOST_UID` (CAM-179) are preserved.

A deterministic test reads the Dockerfile text and asserts AC1+AC2+AC3 (new branch present, group-rename absent, chown + COPY-before-ARG preserved); the existing claude-config-bake.test.ts positional assertions still pass.
`bun run check:all` (typecheck + biome + tests + ratchets) is green.

OPERATOR CEREMONY (requires:operator, hand-filed): a real `docker build --build-arg HOST_UID=501 --build-arg HOST_GID=20 -f .devcontainer/Dockerfile -t cam-worker:latest .` on this macOS host succeeds, and `docker run` shows bun at uid=501 gid=20 with /workspace writable by bun. Folds into the combined CAM-178/183 + CAM-179 + CAM-180 rebuild+verify ceremony.
gotchas: `usermod -g <gid>` requires the group to already exist -- that is why the getent branch is mandatory (you cannot `usermod -g HOST_GID` unconditionally when no group owns that gid).
Renaming a group's NAME with `groupmod -n` does NOT free its GID; the renamed group still owns the number. This is the exact CAM-178 build failure (`groupmod -g 20 bun` -> 'GID 20 already exists').

macOS host gid=20 (staff) collides with the oven/bun:1.2-slim base gid-20 group (conventionally `dialout`, not documented in-repo). This is the real production input: resolveHostIds (src/supervisor/worker-container.ts:144) returns id -g=20, threaded as --build-arg HOST_GID=20.

CI (macos-latest) has NO Docker daemon; all container tests (test/supervisor/*) are argv-builders / Dockerfile-text file-asserts. The real build is UNEXERCISED by the suite -- the deterministic test can only assert Dockerfile TEXT; only the operator ceremony proves the build succeeds and /workspace is writable.

The CAM-179 `COPY ... /home/bun/.claude.json` must remain BEFORE `ARG HOST_UID` so the trailing `chown -R /home/bun` re-owns it to HOST_UID:HOST_GID (guarded by claude-config-bake.test.ts AC3). Do not move the COPY.
The cached cam-worker:latest is the BROKEN 1.16GB image (bun uid=1000, re-home never ran on this host). Do NOT rebuild until this fix lands -- the build WILL fail at the re-home step until then.

Combined operator ceremony: 178/183 (uid=501 gid=20 + /workspace writable) and 179 (zero onboarding/trust prompt) are COUPLED and must be verified together -- the baked .claude.json is only bun-readable after the chown works. CAM-180 folds in.
